page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The hardware configuration includes 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The AMD EPYC processor delivers strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance metrics, such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores, fall into the bottom 25%. Memory subsystem performance is mixed; while cached small-block read bandwidth is weak, uncached large-block read and write bandwidths maintain average tier performance. Cryptographic operations perform at an average level, supported by hardware-accelerated AES, VAES, and SHA instruction sets.

From a resource-density perspective, the n2d-highcpu-4 offers a lean memory profile relative to its processing cores. This makes it a cost-efficient option for workloads that require dedicated CPU cycles but have minimal memory footprints. Due to the weak multi-threaded scaling and low memory capacity, it is poorly suited for memory-intensive databases or heavy multi-threaded compilation. Instead, it is best aligned with lightweight single-threaded tasks, basic web serving, text processing, and low-intensity utility workloads.
